chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends (all) visions' [6:103].

So he said: 'O Abu Hashim! The imaginations of hearts are more subtle than the visions of eyes. You can reach by your imagination al-Sind, al-Hind, and lands you have never entered and do not perceive with your sight — and yet the imaginations of hearts cannot comprehend Him. So how then could the visions of eyes?'

key_terms.الأبصار: Visions/sights — refers to physical eyesight and the act of seeing
key_terms.الأوهام: Imaginations/conceptions — the cognitive faculty of mental visualization and conceptualization
key_terms.السند والهند: Al-Sind and al-Hind — historical regions (Indus Valley and Indian subcontinent), used as examples of distant, unvisited lands
key_terms.يدرك: Comprehends/perceives — to fully grasp or encompass with one's perception

ai.seo_question: Can the human mind or imagination comprehend God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Dawud ibn al-Qasim Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari asks Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Quranic verse 6:103, which states that visions cannot comprehend God. The Imam explains that even the imaginations of the heart — which are more subtle and penetrating than physical sight — are incapable of grasping God's essence. He uses a striking analogy: the mind can conceive distant lands like al-Sind and al-Hind that physical eyes cannot see, yet even these powerful mental faculties cannot encompass God. This is a classical Shia theological argument for God's absolute transcendence beyond all human perception and cognition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Dawood Bin Al Qasim Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘(What about the Verse) [6:103] Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He Comprehends (all) visions?’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Hashim! Imaginations of the hearts are more sharper than the visions of the eyes. You have realised by your imaginations, Al-Sind, and Al-Hind, and the countries which you have not entered into nor seen with your vision, and the imaginations of the heart cannot comprehend Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so how could the visions of the eyes?’
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah has narrated from the person whose name he mentioned from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Dawud ibn al-Qasim abu Hashim al-Ja‘fari who has said the following. “I mentioned the words of Allah , ‘No mortal eyes can see Him, but He can see all eyes. He is All-kind and All-aware.’ [6:103] to Imam abu Ja’far (a.s.).

He said, “O abu Hashim, Awham (mentioned above) of hearts are keener and sharper than the perceptions of the eyes. Through the Awham of the heart you can perceive countries like Sind, Hind (India) and other cities which you have never seen with your eyes. How can your eyes see Him when the Awham of your heart cannot perceive Him?”
